title: vega-window-ops-slate-and-hourly-pressures-jul-2026-draft
content:
Quick summary:

This is the working ops slate for the 'Vega' minimal-impact release window. Purpose: run a controlled, locality-aware rollout of the routing + batching change that reduces per-token cost for short chats. Focus is on short-window canary followed by staged expansion with hour-by-hour pressure checks.

High-level goals:
- Deploy routing/batching change to hosted cluster pool-vega-1.
- Validate latency SLO (p50/p95) and cost-per-token delta on live traffic.
- Ensure graceful fallback to previous routing if quality/regression or capacity issues.

Owners and contacts:
- Release owner: Maya Kapoor (release lead)
- Eng on-call: Ethan Morales (SRE), backup: Liam O'Connor
- Platform: Priya Desai (autoscaler + routing)
- Eval/Quality: Sofia Alvarez
- Slack channel: #release-ops, tag @release-alerts

Rollout clockface (hourly window, UTC):
Note: small-batch run, 4-hour runway, expand only on green telemetry.
- T-02:00 (08:00 UTC) — Final preflight meeting, confirm staffing, backups assigned, confirm PRs merged.
- T-01:00 (09:00 UTC) — Preflight smoke run on staging (short-chat traces), run raw token audit.
- T-00:30 (09:30 UTC) — Bake period; run synthetic load at 40% expected production QPS for 15m.
- T+00:00 (10:00 UTC) — Canary push to 1% traffic on pool-vega-1 (region us-west-2). Tag flows with routing=vega-canary.
- T+00:30 (10:30 UTC) — Rollout pressure check #1: verify latency, error rate, cost sampling. Decision: proceed to 5% or rollback.
- T+01:00 (11:00 UTC) — Expand to 5% for 30m. Telemetry gate.
- T+01:30 (11:30 UTC) — Decision point: 5% -> 20% expansion window. If OK, expand to 20% and monitor for 1h.
- T+02:30 (12:30 UTC) — Expand to 50% (regional) for 45m.
- T+03:15 (13:15 UTC) — Global expansion to 90% if all gates green. Holdback: 10% to allow fast rollback if required.
- T+04:00 (14:00 UTC) — Post-roll stabilization and retrospective sticky notes.

Preflight checklist (must be green before T-00):
- PRs merged: serving-runtime PR#2387 merged & smoke-tested (done)
- Feature flags created: routing.vega.enabled, routing.vega.override (ops knobs)
- Canary pool provisioned: pool-vega-1 (us-west-2), capacity headroom >= 30%
- Alerting: dedicated alert rule created in PagerDuty and Opsgenie for error spike > 0.5% and p95 latency > baseline + 120ms
- Telemetry dashboards: vega-canary dashboard pinned in #release-ops
- Eval prompts: 30 golden prompts loaded to synthetic eval runner (Sofia)
- Customer impact note drafted (customer-success)

Smoke tests (quick list to run during T-01 staging):
- short-chat-flow roundtrip < 200ms p50 in staging
- kv-cache hit behaviour unchanged for prefix cache tests
- streaming response chunking preserved (no truncation)
- token accounting reconciles with billing pipeline sample (sample ids: ve-2026-0001..0005)
- function calling integrations sanity check (5 calls)

Telemetry gates and thresholds (per-hour checks):
- Error rate (5m window): must remain <= 0.5% for canary; <= 0.3% for 20% and above.
- Latency p95: must not regress > 120ms over baseline (baseline measured week of 2026-06-30).
- Quality drift (automated eval): model score delta <= 1.5% on golden prompt set.
- Cost sampling: observed tokens/sec * unit-cost delta tracked vs baseline; expected > 8% cost improvement for short chats.
- KV-cache hit ratio: no drop > 2% vs baseline.

If any gate fails:
- Immediate: flip routing.vega.override -> previous (fast flag) and scale down pool-vega-1 routing to 0%.
- Post-mortem: open Jira RINF-5721-rollback with initial notes in the ticket (owner: Maya).

Rollback playbook (fast path):
1) notify #release-ops with status=rollback and brief reason.
2) set routing.vega.override=false (ops toggle).
3) scale affected pool routing weight to 0% (Priya to run scale command).
4) monitor that errors drop within 5 minutes and p95 returns to baseline within 15 minutes.
5) resume only after RCA and patch or revert merged.

Post-rollout validation (T+04 to T+24):
- 24h after global expansion, run cost regression job over 12h peak period (overnight sample).
- Request platform to produce token-level cost delta report (Finance-visible) and attach to the release ticket.
- QA to run random user conversation checks across 50 live traces.

Release notes (customer-facing draft — short):
Title: Faster short-chat routing (Vega) — July 2026
Summary: We rolled out a routing/batching optimization that reduces per-token unit cost for short-chat sessions while preserving latency and quality. Customers should expect lower inference cost on short sessions and unchanged quality for multi-turn interactions.
Planned impact: Revenue-neutral for current accounts; unit-price reduction visible in billing exports from 2026-07 sample window.
Known limitations: Some very long-prompt flows may see less benefit; if you have heavy KV-cache reliant workloads please contact support.

Open questions (to decide before expansion to 50%):
- Should we enable additional trace sampling for customers on Dedicated to verify cross-tenant isolation? (Priya)
- Acceptable rollback SLO: is 10 minutes max or 5 minutes required for enterprise customers? (CS asks for 5)
- Do we send a pre-release advisory to top 10 customers in us-west-2? (Customer Success)

Action items (owner -> task):
- Maya: finalize customer note and publish to /releases/vega-2026 (draft) by 2026-07-11 (done).
- Priya: confirm autoscaler headroom and run scale soak tomorrow 09:00 UTC (blocked: quota request).
- Ethan: prepare PD escalation playbook and attach runbook link to PD alerts (in progress).
- Sofia: complete golden prompt run and post eval delta by 10:15 UTC on rollout day.
- Liam: standby for rollback drill; confirm access to pool scaling CLI.

Loose notes / heuristics from prior experiments:
- If p95 drifts but errors stable, consider throttling concurrency instead of full rollback to reduce cost shock.
- Maintain a 10% holdback for the first 48 hours to enable quick traffic rebalancing.
- Prefer 'regional ramp' over 'global ramp' when warm caches matter (we keep region-first policy).

Appendix (quick commands and links):
- Scale pool command (ops): opsctl pool set-weight --pool pool-vega-1 --weight 5
- Toggle flag: ffctl set routing.vega.override false --env prod
- Live dashboards: https://telemetry.redwood/boards/vega-canary
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2387
- Rollout ticket: JIRA RINF-5721

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep bake windows slightly longer if any noise in telemetry, we had two noisy 5m spikes last month that resolved in 18m.
- Remember to handshake with Dedicated-support before global ramp: some customers have strict SLA windows and want advance notice.
- Post-release retro: capture how fast rollback path executed and if any throttles impacted downstream services.

End of draft.

-- Maya K.
